newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Firework blitz pierces rain in dazzling HK farewell.
newsitem.headline: Firework blitz pierces rain in dazzling HK farewell.

text.p: As night fell over Hong Kong on Monday for the last time under British rule, a dazzling fireworks display illuminated the sky over Victoria Harbour.

The 20-minute extravaganza, which started 3-3/4 hours before Britain was due to hand Hong Kong back to China at midnight (1600 GMT), drew thousands to the harbour front despite the driving rain which plagued the day's outdoor festivities.
A salvo of shimmering rockets burst into cascades of red, yellow, green and purple and glowed against the backdrop of Hong Kong's famous skyline.
Sparkling fountains filled the sky, drawing cries of delight and applause from the crowd. The wonderment on their faces was lit up by balls of exploding colour.
The mood was festive on the streets, with orderly crowds cheerfully tolerating the rain and the forests of umbrellas that blocked their view. They cheered as the display came to an end.
"It's a memorable occasion," said Yao Ka Chun, a civil servant who brought his five-year-old daughter into the streets to see the fireworks.
"I want her to remember this occasion," he said.
Nearly 20,000 separate explosions had been programmed for the display entitled "A Salute to Hong Kong".

Half of the fireworks were supplied by British firm Kimbolton Fireworks and the other half by Chinese firm Sunny Fireworks in the HK$3.9 million ($500,000) bonanza, sponsored by investment bank ING Barings.
Hong Kong residents were looking forward to a rival extravaganza on Tuesday which was scheduled to include a laser show, a parade of giant lanterns and the largest-ever fireworks display.
Organised by the pro-Beijing Better Hong Kong Foundation to mark Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule, the HK$100 million spectacle would be sponsored by Hong Kong's corporate giants.
"Tomorrow will be a bigger day," said one excited Hong Kong resident. "Tomorrow we will have more fun."
